clue.text: Dish made in France — half of it put in container, but not all

indicators.note: the second half of the French word is shifted into the shortened container

parts.note: fait is the French word for made

indicators.note: only part of the container word is used, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: a jar is a container

explanation.surface: A recipe note about a French dish, half of it spooned into a container that is not quite full.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'it' in 'half of it' is the French word itself: its second half moves into the shortened container while the first half stays in front.
explanation.definitionFit: A fajita is a Mexican-style dish of grilled strips of meat wrapped in a tortilla.

clue.text: Polled live, as many a footballer will have done?

definitions.note: polled can mean with the head cut off or lopped

parts.note: to live is to be, to exist

parts.words: as many a footballer will have done
parts.note: footballers often have headed the ball

explanation.surface: A question about footballers who have been polled for their opinion while still playing.
explanation.walkthrough: Polled looks like voting; its older sense is having the head (or horns) removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Polled once meant cropped at the head, so a polled person has had the head taken off.

clue.text: Capital chap, a fellow in solitary?

indicators.note: the fellow word is placed inside the word for a solitary person

parts.note: a solitary person is a loner
a don is a university fellow

explanation.surface: A man from the big city is pictured as a lonely academic in solitary confinement.
explanation.definitionFit: A man from the British capital city is a native or resident of that city.

clue.text: Almost nothing dull in this resort

indicators.note: almost all the word for nothing is used, its last letter dropped

parts.note: zero is nothing
matt means dull, without shine

explanation.surface: A complaint that there is next to nothing dull about this holiday spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Zermatt is a Swiss ski resort beneath the Matterhorn.

clue.text: Character once left after British engineer

indicators.note: the character and left letters come after the British letter

parts.note: a rune is a character of an ancient alphabet

explanation.surface: A historic figure departs, following a British engineer.
explanation.definitionFit: Isambard Kingdom Brunel was a famous Victorian engineer of bridges, railways and ships.

clue.text: Moving towards border

definitions.meaning: a trim or fringe along an edge

explanation.surface: Someone shuffling up to a frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: inching gradually forward, and a decorative trim along a rim.

clue.text: Fan out when dancing in spring

indicators.note: dancing letters move around, so these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dancer spreads out a fan in springtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when dancing' looks like part of the scene but is the anagram signal; 'spring' reads as the season, yet it is a source of water.
explanation.definitionFit: A fountain is a spring of water, a source where water jets or wells up.

clue.text: Mouth about type of surgery that's not unknown

parts.note: ca, short for circa, means about

indicators.note: an unknown in algebra is y, so that letter is removed

parts.note: keyhole surgery is minimally invasive surgery

explanation.surface: Sounds like an operation on the mouth by a well-known kind of surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: In maths x, y and z are unknowns; here Y goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Cakehole is British slang for the mouth, as in 'shut your cakehole'.

clue.text: Perhaps set back by rheumatoid arthritis to an extent

indicators.note: set back means the letters found are read in the reverse direction
only part of the phrase is used, the letters lying within the two words

explanation.surface: Someone is set back by a painful joint condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to an extent' picks OIDAR from rheumatOID ARthritis; 'back' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A set is a broadcast receiver, of which a wireless is one example.

clue.text: Cable in Wiltshire, stripped of core

indicators.note: the inner letters of the county name are removed, leaving the ends

explanation.surface: A cable in a West Country county has had its central wires exposed.
explanation.walkthrough: Wiltshire is an English county; 'stripped of core' removes LTSHI, leaving WI and RE.
explanation.definitionFit: A cable is a length of conducting metal strand, insulated or bare.

clue.text: Size of papers backing remark in report

indicators.note: backing means the papers word is turned round

parts.note: ID means identity papers

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the word is said aloud

parts.note: to mention is to remark

explanation.surface: Newspapers supporting a comment made in a report on size.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns ID into DI; 'in report' gives the sound of MENTION, written MENSION.
explanation.definitionFit: A dimension is a measurement such as length or width, a measure of extent.

clue.text: Excuse signal — charge to be overturned

indicators.note: overturned means the combined words are read backwards

parts.note: a nod is a signal
a rap is a criminal charge

explanation.surface: A legal plea: a hint that the charge will be thrown out on appeal.
explanation.definitionFit: To pardon is to forgive or let off, which is what to excuse means.

clue.text: Closure of mainline journey section in public transport message

indicators.note: the first letters go inside the transport word

parts.note: a tram is a form of public transport

indicators.note: the closure of a word is its final letter

parts.note: a leg is a stage of a journey

explanation.surface: A notice about a line closure on part of a rail journey.
explanation.definitionFit: A telegram is a message sent by telegraph and delivered on paper.

clue.text: Death of Venus and Adonis, originally when 2?

indicators.note: 2 is beheaded: with each word's head off, the original letters are their second ones

explanation.surface: A query about the deaths in Shakespeare's poem Venus and Adonis.
explanation.walkthrough: 2-down is BEHEADED; beheaded, the three words begin E, N, D.
explanation.definitionFit: An end is a death, the finish of a life.

clue.text: Straggling agent hiding international article in Berlin

indicators.note: the agent word conceals the others within it

parts.note: a spy is a secret agent
der is a German definite article

explanation.surface: A stray spy conceals a foreign object in Berlin.
explanation.definitionFit: Spidery handwriting is thin and sprawling, with long irregular strokes.

clue.text: A girl having the edge in writing?

indicators.note: the edge word is placed inside the writing word

parts.note: prose is ordinary written language
a rim is an edge

explanation.surface: A girl with the upper hand in her written work.
explanation.definitionFit: Primrose is a female given name, taken from the yellow spring flower.

clue.text: The Elusive Pimpernel, ultimately a slippery sort

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of each word

explanation.surface: The hero of a famous novel is a hard man to catch.
explanation.walkthrough: The Scarlet Pimpernel is the elusive hero of Baroness Orczy's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: An eel is a long slimy fish, and a byword for a person hard to pin down.

clue.text: Dullard in squat almost stifling noise

indicators.note: the shortened word smothers the noise word inside it
almost all of the word is used, the last letter dropped

parts.note: squat means short and fat, pudgy
din is noise

explanation.surface: A slow-witted person squatting down and muffling a sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A pudding is British slang for a stupid or sluggish person, a lump.

clue.text: Tanned 2 in need of a wash

indicators.note: 2-down is beheaded, so the first letter is removed

parts.note: to have sunbathed is to have lain in the sun to tan

explanation.surface: Someone sunburnt and grubby after a beach day.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference to 2-down tells you to remove the head, the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has not had a bath is dirty and wants cleaning.

clue.text: After switching components, stop working where gas flows?

indicators.note: the two parts of the phrase change places

parts.note: to wind down is to stop working, to relax

explanation.surface: An engineer swaps parts and shuts down, asking where the gas goes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After switching components' swaps WIND and DOWN. The question mark flags the flatulent hint in 'gas'.
explanation.definitionFit: Gas released in the open drifts in the direction the breeze blows it.

clue.text: Appendix with questions bring something to mind?

parts.note: PS, a postscript, is an addition at the end of a letter
and means with
Q is short for question, so QS is questions

explanation.surface: Adding questions at the end makes one think.
explanation.definitionFit: To mind your Ps and Qs is the idiom for watching your manners.

clue.text: Lacking connection, wife apparently in a good mood

parts.note: ire is anger, so someone without ire seems content

explanation.surface: A cut-off wife who seems cheerful all the same.
explanation.walkthrough: 'apparently' flags a made-up word: IRE-LESS, without anger.
explanation.definitionFit: Wireless technology works with no cables or physical link.

clue.text: They twirl in topless underwear

indicators.note: the top, the first letter, is removed

parts.note: a teddy is a one-piece undergarment for women

explanation.surface: Dancers spinning around in skimpy lingerie.
explanation.definitionFit: Eddies are swirls of water or air that spin round in circles.

clue.text: Old stone hotel, one needing renovation

indicators.note: renovation rebuilds, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: An old stone hotel needing to be done up.
explanation.definitionFit: An eolith is a crudely chipped flint thought to be among the earliest tools.

clue.text: Sportsman left in enclosure

indicators.note: the left letter goes inside the enclosure word

parts.note: a bower is a shady leafy retreat enclosed by trees

explanation.surface: An athlete stays behind in a pen.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowler is a cricketer who delivers the ball, and also a player of bowls.

clue.text: Call into East London, primarily for some hard stuff

indicators.note: the call word goes into the other letters
primarily means the first letter of the word

parts.note: to name is to call

explanation.surface: A call to the East End of London for a stiff drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some hard stuff' looks like strong liquor; it is the coating on teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: Enamel is the hard glossy coating on teeth, and a hard paint or glaze.

clue.text: Mars case for enrolment on left-wing scheme

indicators.note: the outer letters come on after the other pieces

parts.note: red means left-wing, socialist
a plan is a scheme

indicators.note: the case is the outside, so the first and last letters

explanation.surface: An argument for joining a socialist programme.
explanation.definitionFit: Mars is called this because of its rusty reddish colour.

clue.text: How, perhaps, 25 put on weight

indicators.note: the hat goes on after the weight letter

parts.note: 25-across is bowler, a type of hat

explanation.surface: Someone asks how a cricketer has put on weight.
explanation.definitionFit: Both 'how?' and 'what?' serve as exclamations asking someone to repeat themselves.

clue.text: Gentle 9 or 22 hosting you patronisingly

indicators.note: the set word holds the other inside it

parts.note: 9 is radio and 22 is wireless, both called a set
'we', as in 'how are we today?', is a patronising way to address you

explanation.surface: A gentle broadcaster talking down to the listener.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweet means kind and mild-mannered, soft in temper.

clue.text: Company woman who governs, inter alia, social workers

parts.note: a queen is a monarch who reigns
a bee is one among the social insects that work in a colony

explanation.surface: A businesswoman runs the office among social workers.
explanation.definitionFit: A queen bee is a dominant woman in a group or firm, bossing the others.
